findings.title: Cleanup can delete an object while its approval transaction is still in flight
findings.scenario: Completion independently commits a cleanup intent due in five minutes, writes the public image or sealed document, then pauses before its outer transaction commits. After the deadline, another instance runs cleanup. Its ordinary SELECT sees the previously committed media row, which does not yet reference the new key, deletes the object and marks cleanup DONE. Completion subsequently commits APPROVED with the deleted key.
findings.expected: Cleanup must exclude objects belonging to an in-flight approval, regardless of transaction duration.
findings.actual: The five-minute delay is the only barrier protecting an uncommitted approval. The reference check does not lock or synchronize with the media transaction, and complete() declares no transaction timeout enforcing completion before that deadline.
findings.evidence: MediaService.java:126-127 opens the outer transaction; :199-202 and :209-212 independently enqueue cleanup before writing and committing approval. MediaCleanup.java:63-65 commits the intent with REQUIRES_NEW; :88-99 selects due intents and checks only committed references; :105-107 deletes and finishes without coordinating with the approval's asset lock.
findings.suggested_fix: Coordinate cleanup with the owning media transaction through a consistent locking or attempt-ownership protocol. A fixed delay alone cannot prove an approval is no longer in flight.
findings.repro_test: With synthetic storage and separate PostgreSQL transactions, pause completion after object write but before commit, advance the cleanup clock beyond five minutes, and run cleanup from another transaction. Resume completion and assert every committed APPROVED key remains readable. Repeat for public variants and sealed documents. Static scenario; not executed.
